intro.h2: Richmond families keep calling the same company back
paragraphs: Custom Kitchens has been doing kitchen remodeling in Richmond, VA for over 65 years, and the Hendrick family still runs it from the same showroom. The work covers kitchens, bathrooms and built-in cabinetry, planned by certified designers and installed by experienced craftsmen.

Many clients are not on their first project. One Google reviewer had the firm remodel his kitchen, then came back years later for the primary bath. A Libbie and Grove client wrote that every time they move, they call Custom Kitchens for the renovation. The company's promise is short: listen, do it right and do it on time.

services.h2: What Custom Kitchens designs and installs

items.name: Kitchen Renovations
items.blurb: Full kitchen renovations planned from layout to hardware by a certified designer, then installed by the CKI team from tear-out to final install. The showroom carries brands such as Wolf, Sub-Zero, Bosch and Omega Cabinetry, so you can compare appliances and cabinets you won't find at a big box store.

image.alt: Old Meets New on Hanover kitchen in Richmond with a navy island, white cabinetry, stainless built-in refrigerator and long open floor plan

items.name: Bath Renovations
items.blurb: Primary baths, hall baths and powder rooms designed with the same care as a kitchen, from vanity cabinetry and tile to fixtures and lighting. Projects range from a sparkling primary retreat with a freestanding tub to small powder rooms with patterned wallpaper and brass fittings.

image.alt: Richmond primary bathroom remodel with a walnut vanity, white quartz top and freestanding soaking tub

items.name: Built-In Cabinetry
items.blurb: Home offices, bars, mudroom storage and other built-ins made with the same cabinet lines and installers as a kitchen. The team walks clients through one process for every project, which the firm says lowers stress, shortens construction time and gives the best result.

image.alt: Built-in home office in Tarrington with gray-stained cabinetry, open shelves, a desk with under-cabinet lighting and a black counter

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons Richmond homeowners give for choosing CKI

items.title: Three generations in one showroom
items.text: Richard Hendrick took over from his father, the founder, in 1986. His sons Kyle, Carter and Curtis now work as designers and managers, so the family name is on every job.

items.title: Certified designers on staff
items.text: The team includes Certified Kitchen Designers such as Richard Hendrick and Allison Stowers, along with licensed contractors and experienced craftsmen. A certified designer is always on site at the showroom.

items.title: A price you can hold them to
items.text: A North Chesterfield client wrote that designer Kyle offered layout and price options, then 'We determined a price and worked to it and stuck to it!' The expected price creep never came.

items.title: Recognized by local peers
items.text: The firm lists Contractor of the Year honors for 2017 through 2020 and 2023 and PRO Awards from 2022 to 2025, and it belongs to the Central Virginia PRO chapter and the NKBA.

about.text: Richard Hendrick has spent his whole career in the family business. He started as a carpenter's helper in high school and college, learning how kitchens are actually built. His father, the founder of Custom Kitchens, was his mentor and taught the client-first approach the company still runs on. Richard became president in 1986 and is a Certified Kitchen Designer known for award-winning designs. He has since brought in the third generation: Kyle as vice president and designer, Carter as designer and Curtis, a former installation manager, as vice president of operations.

image.alt: Richard Hendrick, CKD, president of Custom Kitchens Inc in Richmond, VA

process.h2: Planning, design and installation, in that order

steps.title: Visit the showroom
steps.text: Stop by Horsepen Road to get inspired and meet a designer. No appointment is needed, and a private design session is free.

steps.title: Planning
steps.text: Your designer listens to your needs, discusses the project and budget, proposes ideas and explains your options.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: After a design deposit, you get drafts and concepts, pick finishes and colors, review perspective drawings and make revisions.

steps.title: Installation
steps.text: Once the contract is signed, materials are ordered and received before construction, a temporary kitchen is set up, then demo and installation begin.

steps.title: Start living
steps.text: The finished room is yours to enjoy, and the team stays available for warranty service after the job.

service_area.h2: Where we handle kitchen remodeling in Richmond, VA and nearby
service_area.text: The showroom is at 6412 Horsepen Road in Richmond. Client stories on the site come from the Near West End, Windsor Farms, Libbie and Grove, Rothesay Circle and Stratford Hills in the city, from Henrico and the Wellesley area, and from Chesterfield and North Chesterfield. Recent projects include a Tarrington kitchen and a farmhouse by the Rappahannock. If your neighborhood is not listed, call and ask.

faq.h2: Questions we hear in the Horsepen Road showroom

items.q: Do I need an appointment to visit the showroom?
items.a: No. The showroom is open to the public Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, and a certified designer is always on site. After-hours appointments are available on request. If you want private time with a designer, leave your details and the team will set up a complimentary design session.

items.q: Which brands can I see in person?
items.a: The showroom features many high-end finishes and hardware lines plus brands such as Wolf, Sub-Zero, Bosch and Omega Cabinetry. These are products you usually cannot find at a big box store, and seeing them side by side makes choosing cabinets and appliances much easier.

items.q: When do I pay a deposit?
items.a: Planning comes first: your designer listens, discusses the project and budget and explains your options. A design deposit starts the design phase of drafts, finish selections, perspectives and revisions. You sign the construction contract only after the design is done, and materials arrive before demolition starts.

items.q: Will I have a working kitchen during the remodel?
items.a: Custom Kitchens sets up a temporary kitchen as part of the installation phase, so you can still make coffee and simple meals while the old kitchen comes out. Ordering and receiving materials before construction begins also keeps the time without a kitchen as short as possible.

items.q: What happens if something needs fixing later?
items.a: The company handles warranty claims. One Google reviewer bought a home with a kitchen Custom Kitchens had recently renovated, and said Curtis and Blake went above and beyond when a warranty issue came up. Ask your designer for the written warranty terms for your project.
